plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Fragrant blossoms open on bare branches while winter still grips the landscape. The flowers are delicate, five-petaled and sweetly spiced. They appear in gardens, shrines and orchards, where they signal that spring is on its way.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January through March, often peaking in mid-February to early March
plants.location: Japan, especially the Kantō and Kansai regions, including Mito and Kyoto
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms were celebrated in Japan before cherry blossoms became the national favorite. The fruit is pickled as umeboshi and also used to make plum wine.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: This is the largest of the proteas. Its flower head is a bowl-shaped crown of silky, pointed bracts around a center like a fuzzy pincushion. It grows on rocky fynbos slopes and has a bold, sculptural look.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late winter through spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from about autumn to early summer. Peak flowering is usually August to November, and some blooms appear in summer.
plants.location: Fynbos regions of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. It has thick, fire-adapted stems that resprout after bushfires.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs bear rose-like or peony-like blooms against dark, shiny leaves. The flowers appear in winter, when little else in the garden is blooming.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with a strong peak in February in mild climates
plants.location: Gardens in the southeastern United States, such as Georgia and the Carolinas, and in Japan and western Europe
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. In Japan it is called tsubaki, and its seeds are pressed for a prized hair and skin oil.
